info.title: TrafficMorph API
info.description:
Programmatic access to TrafficMorph traffic profiles, runs, history, and domain verification. Designed for CI integration: trigger a run, wait for completion, fetch the regression verdict, and gate the build on the result.

**Authentication.** All `/api/v1/*` endpoints require an API key. Provision keys in the in-app settings page; send each request with either:
  * `X-Api-Key: tm_<key>` (recommended for CI scripts), or
  * `Authorization: Bearer tm_<key>` (recommended for SDKs).

**Plan gating (CLOUD).** On the hosted service, the public API is a TEAM+ feature â SOLO accounts receive HTTP 403 with `code=PLAN_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`. In **SELF_HOSTED** installs (`app.deployment-mode=SELF_HOSTED`), every endpoint is available to every authenticated user regardless of stored plan tier.

**Rate limiting.** Each API key has plan-tier-derived limits enforced by `ApiRateLimitFilter`. Rate-limited responses are HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header.

**Fetching this spec programmatically.** Always use the explicit group URLs `/v3/api-docs/v1` (JSON) or `/v3/api-docs.yaml/v1` (YAML â note the `.yaml` extension is on the BASE path, not the group). The default un-grouped URLs `/v3/api-docs` and `/v3/api-docs.yaml` are intentionally blocked â 401 for unauthenticated callers and 403 for authenticated ones. They would otherwise scan every internal controller in the boot context and leak admin / auth / billing endpoints. Configure SDK generators (`openapi-generator-cli`, `oapi-codegen`, etc.) to point at the v1 group URL directly.

tags.name: Variables sets
tags.description: CSV-style attached variables â sampled per-request to make profiles replay traffic with realistic per-request data (authenticated tokens, parameterized URLs, etc.). Pairs with the capture-import flow that auto-creates these from production traffic samples.

tags.name: Domains
tags.description: Domain ownership verification. Profiles can only target hosts the user has proven they own â via DNS TXT record or HTTP-token challenge.

tags.name: Captures
tags.description: JSONL traffic-capture import. Preview a captured trace and atomically materialise detected endpoints as TrafficMorph profiles + variables sets. Useful for bootstrapping a load test from real production traffic without hand-modelling the request shape.

tags.name: Profiles
tags.description: Traffic profile CRUD. A profile holds the target endpoint, RPS curve, request body / headers, optional scripts, optional schedule, and alert policy that drive each run.

tags.name: Runs
tags.description: Start, stop, pause, and resume traffic runs for a saved profile.

tags.name: Regions
tags.description: Dispatch regions a run can originate from.

tags.name: History
tags.description: Read-only access to past runs. Carries per-run latency / throughput / error metrics and the auto-comparison verdict against the selected baseline â the key endpoint for CI quality gates.

get.description: Returns the full profile including its schedule (if any) and current run status. Returns 400 if the profile doesn't exist or belongs to a different user â the service throws `IllegalArgumentException("Profile not found")` for both cases, and the global handler maps that to 400.

200.description: Profile found.

400.description: Profile not found or not owned by this user. Body: `{"error":"Profile not found"}`.

put.description:
Ownership-checks the profile by path id, then updates that specific row in place. The body's `name` is the new value to store, not a lookup key â even if it matches a different profile's name, only the path-id row is mutated. (The save service has both an id-based and a name-based code path; the controller pins the path id on the save request so the id-based branch runs.)

Name uniqueness is NOT enforced server-side: PUT will happily produce a duplicate-named pair under the same user. Subsequent name-keyed operations (POST `/profiles` upsert) would then resolve to the most-recently-created duplicate, which is rarely what the caller wanted. Clients that care about uniqueness (e.g. the MCP server's `tm_update_profile`) should pre-flight a `GET /profiles` and reject renames that would collide.

The schedule block, if present, replaces any existing schedule for the profile; omitting it leaves the current schedule untouched. Likewise `variablesSetIds`, `region`, `readinessUrl` and `interpolationMode` keep their stored values when omitted; every other field is replaced from the body.

400.description: Profile not found / not owned by this user, OR validation failure on the request body. Body: `{"error":"<reason>"}`.

200.description: Profile updated; response carries the full updated entity.

delete.description: Removes the profile and its associated schedule. Any in-flight run is cancelled. Run history is retained â only the profile definition is removed.

400.description: Profile not found or not owned by this user. Body: `{"error":"Profile not found"}`.

get.description: Returns metadata for every variables set owned by the API key's user. The raw CSV content is intentionally omitted from list responses â use `GET /{id}` for a single set's metadata, or download the CSV via the in-app UI endpoint if you need row-level inspection.

200.description: List of variables sets; may be empty.

post.summary: Create a variables set from inline CSV content
post.description:
CSV is uploaded as a string in the JSON body (NOT as a multipart file). Size-capped at the parser's `MAX_BYTES` â for larger sets, downsample client-side before uploading.

The CSV's first row is the column header. Columns whose names match `$$macro$$` placeholders in the profile's URL / body / headers get substituted per-request at run time. An optional special column `weight` (case-insensitive) makes rows pickable with a probability proportional to its value â useful for replaying real traffic distributions.

Sampling modes (mirrors `VariablesSet.SamplingMode`):
  - `ROW`: one row sampled per request; ALL columns substituted from that row. Preserves cross-column correlations. REQUIRES a `weight` column.
  - `COLUMN`: each column sampled INDEPENDENTLY per request, producing uncorrelated combinations across columns. A shared `weight` column acts as the default weight; per-column `{col}_weight` columns override for individual ones. Weights are optional.
  - `SEQUENTIAL`: rows walked in CSV order; one row per request, wrapping after the last. Weights ignored. Combined with a derived RPS curve, reproduces both the input distribution AND the timing of the original capture.

400.description: Validation failure: blank name, missing CSV, malformed CSV, exceeded size cap, exceeded per-user quota, etc.

get.description: Returns lightweight summaries (id, name, duration, last-run info) for every profile owned by the API key's user. Order: most-recently-updated first.

200.description: List of profile summaries; may be empty.

post.summary: Create or upsert a profile by name (optionally with schedule)
post.description:
Saves a traffic profile keyed by `name`. If a profile with the same name already exists for this user, **it is updated in place rather than rejected** â the underlying service is an upsert. Treat this endpoint as idempotent-by-name. Use `PUT /{id}` instead if you need to update a profile and rename it at the same time.

If the request body includes a `schedule` block, a `ScheduledRun` is created or replaced in the same logical transaction.

On an upsert, `variablesSetIds`, `region`, `readinessUrl` and `interpolationMode` keep their stored values when omitted (null); every other field is replaced from the body.

400.description: Validation failure: missing required fields, invalid URL, blocked target host, per-user profile limit reached on new creation, init/cleanup scripts on a non-TEAM plan, etc.

201.description: Profile saved; response carries the full saved entity. Returned for BOTH freshly created profiles AND name-upsert updates of existing profiles.

post.summary: Stop the in-flight run for a profile
post.description: Resets the profile's run state. Fully idempotent â succeeds with `status="IDLE"` even when no run is currently in flight and even when the profile id is unknown to the user (the run-state store is keyed by user+profile and silently no-ops on misses). Any in-flight dispatch loops cancel within a tick.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the profile whose in-flight run to stop.

200.description: Stop signal acknowledged; response carries the post-stop status (`IDLE` after a successful stop).

post.summary: Start a run for a saved profile
post.description: Loads the profile by id, builds a run-start request from its configured RPS curve / endpoint / scripts, and dispatches it. Tagged `triggeredBy="api"` so it can be distinguished from UI- and schedule-triggered runs in history. Enforces the user's request-usage quota before starting. To set a dispatch region or history tags for the run, use `POST /runs` instead.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the saved profile to run.

400.description: Run could not start. Covers: profile not found / not owned, concurrent-run limit reached, target domain not verified, init-script failure, invalid `targetUrl`, init/cleanup scripts on a non-TEAM plan, or any other validation error. Body: `{"error":"<reason>"}`.

409.description: Monthly request-usage quota exhausted. Body carries `code=USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED`, plus `usedRequests` / `includedRequests` / `usagePercent` / `upgradeUrl`. Distinct from the per-profile concurrent-run cap, which is a 400.

200.description: Run started; response carries the run id and current status.

post.summary: Start a run with per-run options
post.description: Same as `POST /start`, plus an optional dispatch `region` and history `tags` for this run. Without a body it behaves exactly like `/start`: dispatched locally, no tags. (A separate operation so the existing `start` signature in generated clients stays unchanged.)

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the saved profile to run.

409.description: Monthly request-usage quota exhausted; same body as `/start`.

400.description: Same causes as `/start`, plus an unknown or plan-restricted `region` and invalid `tags`. Body: `{"error":"<reason>"}`.

200.description: Run started; response carries the run id and current status.

post.description: Continues dispatch from where `/pause` left off. The RPS curve and any SEQUENTIAL variables-set cursors retain their pre-pause position. **Not** idempotent in the absence-of-state case â unlike `/pause` and `/stop`, calling `/resume` without an in-flight or paused run is a client error.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the profile whose paused run to resume.

200.description: Resume acknowledged; response carries the post-resume status.

400.description: No run to resume (none in flight or already completed). Body: `{"error":"No active run to resume for selected profile"}` or `{"error":"Run already completed. Start a new run or reset."}`.

post.summary: Pause the in-flight run for a profile
post.description: Suspends dispatch. The run retains its position on the RPS curve and can be resumed via `/resume`. Idempotent â when no run is currently in flight the response is `status="IDLE"` rather than an error, so a CI workflow can call `/pause` without first checking state. Useful when a step needs to inspect intermediate metrics without losing progress.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the profile whose in-flight run to pause.

200.description: Pause acknowledged; response carries the post-pause status (`PAUSED` for active runs, `IDLE` when there was nothing to pause).

get.summary: List the user's domains and their verification status
get.description: Returns all domains the user has added, with each domain's current verification state (`PENDING` / `VERIFIED`) and the challenge tokens still in play.

200.description: List of domains; may be empty.

post.summary: Register a new domain for verification
post.description: Idempotent. On first call, generates the verification token and creates the record. On subsequent calls for the same `(user, domain)`, returns the existing record with the same token â clients can safely retry without producing duplicates. The response carries the challenge values the user must install before calling `/verify/dns` or `/verify/http`.

400.description: Blank domain, missing user, or any other validation failure. Body: `{"error":"<reason>"}`.

201.description: Domain ready for verification. Returned for BOTH a freshly created record AND an already-registered one (idempotent contract). Same token in both cases.

post.description: Fetches `https://{domain}/.well-known/trafficmorph-verify.txt` (falling back to HTTP if HTTPS fails) and matches its body against the challenge token. Alternative to DNS verification for users without DNS control. **On miss**, returns 400 with a remediation message â same fail-fast contract as `/verify/dns`.

400.description: Verification failed. Covers: domain id not owned by this user, file not found, file present but token mismatch, or fetch failed over both HTTPS and HTTP. Body carries the expected URL + token in the error message.

200.description: Domain verified (file matched, or already verified prior to this call).

post.description: Looks up the configured TXT record at `_trafficmorph-verify.{domain}` and matches it against the challenge value issued when the domain was added. On match, the domain flips to `VERIFIED` and can be used as a profile target. **On miss**, returns 400 with a remediation message â the call is treated as a failed verification attempt rather than a polling no-op, so CI flows fail fast instead of looping on always-`PENDING` 200s.

200.description: Domain verified (record matched, or already verified prior to this call).

400.description: Verification failed. Covers: domain id not owned by this user, no matching TXT record found, or DNS lookup failed. Body carries the expected TXT name + token in the error message so the user can fix and retry.

post.summary: Import selected endpoints from a JSONL capture as profiles
post.description:
Atomic commit. Re-derives the analysis from the uploaded file (no server-side state is kept between `/analyse` and `/import`), picks the groups named in the `selections` JSON, and persists each one as a TrafficMorph profile â plus a variables set whenever the group has variable positions. Either every selection lands or none. Re-upload the same JSONL file you analysed; selections key by `(method, urlSkeleton)` so re-analysis matches the same groups.

**Name collisions are NOT errors.** If a chosen `profileName` is already taken for this user, the importer auto-suffixes with `(2)`, `(3)`, â¦ until unique. The created entity in the response carries the final name, so the client can show what actually landed. (Same convention applies to variables-set names.)

parameters.name: selections
parameters.description: JSON string with the import selections. Shape: `{"groups":[{"method":"POST","urlSkeleton":"https://api.example.com/api/bid","profileName":"Bid endpoint"}]}`. Sent as a plain multipart text field (not `application/json`) so all HTTP clients including browser `FormData` work without content-type acrobatics.

file.description: JSONL traffic-capture file â the same file you analysed.

413.description: Upload exceeds the multipart size limit.

200.description: Import complete; response carries created-profile ids (with the final, possibly auto-suffixed names), any selections skipped because no group in the re-analysis matched, and non-fatal warnings.

400.description: Missing file, missing/invalid `selections` JSON, capture failed to re-parse, or per-user profile limit reached.

post.summary: Analyse a JSONL capture and preview the proposed profiles
post.description: Uploads a JSONL traffic capture and returns a structured preview â per detected endpoint: the proposed URL skeleton, derived RPS curve, extracted URL + body variables (with cardinality buckets and sample values), and a few sample request URLs. **No state is persisted.** Pair with `/import` to commit the selections you want.

file.description: JSONL traffic-capture file. Each line is one captured request (method, url, timestamp, optional headers + body).

200.description: Analysis complete; response carries one group per detected endpoint.

400.description: Missing or empty file, or capture failed to parse.

413.description: Upload exceeds the multipart size limit (default 120 MB).

get.summary: Get a single variables set's metadata
get.description: Returns id, name, sampling mode, macro columns, optional weight column, row count, size, and timestamps. Raw CSV content NOT included â that's a separate concern served only by the in-app UI endpoint.

400.description: Variables set not found or not owned by this user. The service throws `IllegalArgumentException("Variables set not found")` for both cases. Body: `{"error":"Variables set not found"}`.

200.description: Variables set found.

delete.description: Removes the set. **Fails fast (HTTP 400) if any profile still has this set attached** â the response body's error message names the referencing profile(s) so the caller can detach them first. There is NO auto-detach: the deliberate design is to make accidental attachment loss visible. To delete an attached set, either (a) detach via `tm_update_profile` / the UI on each referencing profile and then retry the delete, or (b) delete the referencing profiles themselves if they're no longer needed.

400.description: Set not found, not owned by this user, OR still attached to one or more profiles. The error body for the still-attached case has shape `{"error":"Can't delete 'name' â still attached to profile(s): A, B, .... Detach it from those profiles first."}`.

patch.description: Changes only the display name. The CSV content, mode, and attached-profile relationships are untouched.

200.description: Variables set renamed.

400.description: Set not found or new name invalid (blank / too long).

patch.summary: Change the sampling mode of an existing variables set
patch.description: Switches between any of the three modes (`ROW`, `COLUMN`, `SEQUENTIAL`) without re-uploading the CSV. Most common use: a capture-import-created set lands in `ROW` mode by default; flip it to `SEQUENTIAL` for ordered replay that reproduces the original traffic order, or to `COLUMN` for uncorrelated per-column sampling. The server re-parses the stored CSV with the target mode and 400s if incompatible (e.g. switching to `ROW` on a CSV with no `weight` column). See the POST endpoint description for the full mode semantics.

200.description: Mode changed.

400.description: Set not found or mode invalid.

get.summary: List the dispatch regions available to this user
get.description: Region codes accepted by a profile's `region` and by the `region` field of `POST /api/v1/profiles/{id}/start`. The local (in-process) region is listed whenever it's enabled. Remote regions appear only when the plan allows multi-region dispatch and at least one agent is connected.

200.description: Enabled regions, ordered by region code.

get.summary: Get the live status of a profile's run
get.description: Returns the in-flight run's progress: status, elapsed time, requests sent, response-code counts, current RPS and the last minute of 5-second buckets (RPS, outcome ratios, latency percentiles). Poll this instead of subscribing to the WebSocket. `IDLE` when nothing is running; once a run finishes, its final metrics and verdict are in `/api/v1/history`.

200.description: Current run state.

400.description: Profile not found or not owned by this user. Body: `{"error":"Profile not found"}`.

get.summary: List past runs with optional filters
get.description: Paginated run history. Filters narrow by profile, trigger source (`api` / `manual` / `scheduled`), region, regression verdict (`PASS` / `WARN` / `FAIL` / `NO_BASELINE`), tag, and date range. All filters are AND-combined. Use `autoVerdict=FAIL` to fetch the runs a CI gate should care about.

200.description: Page of run summaries plus pagination metadata.

get.summary: Get a single run's full detail
get.description: Returns the run's complete metric set: response-code distribution, latency quantiles, RPS / latency time series, secondary stats from response scripts, the auto-comparison snapshot against baseline, and the verdict reasoning. This is the endpoint a CI step polls after `/profiles/{id}/start` to decide pass/fail.

200.description: Run found; response carries every captured metric.

400.description: Run not found or not owned by this user. The service throws `IllegalArgumentException("Run history not found")` for both cases, and the global handler maps that to 400. Body: `{"error":"Run history not found"}`.

get.summary: Compare two runs of the same profile
get.description: The comparison the web UI's compare view shows. `runA` in the response is always the more recent run. Latency p50 / p95 / p99 are compared with a t-test over the runs' time buckets; success, error and per-status-code counts with a bootstrap against the profile's historical run-to-run deltas. `significant` flags a change unlikely to be noise.

parameters.name: runB
parameters.description: Run-history id of the other run.

400.description: Same run twice, or runs from different profiles.

404.description: A run doesn't exist or isn't owned by this user.

200.description: Comparison computed.

delete.description: Deletes the domain and its challenges. Profiles targeting this domain remain saved but won't be runnable until another verified domain covers the target host.

400.description: Domain not found or not owned by this user. Body: `{"error":"Domain not found"}`.

variablesSetIds.description: Attached variables-set ids; their CSV columns fill `$$column$$` macros. Null keeps the current attachments; `[]` detaches all.

items.description: Attached variables-set ids; their CSV columns fill `$$column$$` macros. Null keeps the current attachments; `[]` detaches all.

region.description: Default dispatch region code for web-UI and scheduled runs (see `GET /api/v1/regions`). Null keeps the current value; `""` clears it (local).

readinessUrl.description: URL checked before a scheduled run fires; while it isn't ready the run is postponed (up to 15 minutes) or skipped. Null keeps the current value; `""` clears it.

interpolationMode.description: How RPS is interpolated between curve points: `SPLINE` (smooth) or `LINEAR`. Null keeps the current mode (`SPLINE` for new profiles).

ApiProfileRequest.description: Create or update payload for a traffic profile. The `points` array defines the RPS curve (one or more (x,y) coordinates where x is seconds since run-start and y is target RPS). The optional `schedule` block atomically creates or replaces an automated schedule alongside the profile.

ApiProfileResponse.description: Full profile view: stored configuration + attached schedule (when present) + the current run status (`idle` / `running` / `paused`). Returned from create / get / update calls so the client never needs follow-up roundtrips to fetch related state.

region.description: Dispatch region code for this run (see `GET /api/v1/regions`). Omitted: dispatched locally, like `/start`; the profile's default `region` is not applied.

tags.description: Tags stored on the run's history row, e.g. a release or commit id; filter with `GET /api/v1/history?tag=`. Normalized to lowercase `[a-z0-9._-]`. At most 20 tags of 60 characters.

items.description: Tags stored on the run's history row, e.g. a release or commit id; filter with `GET /api/v1/history?tag=`. Normalized to lowercase `[a-z0-9._-]`. At most 20 tags of 60 characters.

ApiRunStartRequest.description: Optional per-run settings. The whole body may be omitted.

runId.description: In-memory run id (matches `runId` on the history row); null when idle.

region.description: Dispatch region code; null when idle.

elapsedSeconds.description: Seconds of the RPS curve played so far (paused time excluded).

additionalProperties.description: HTTP status code â responses so far.

responseCodeCounts.description: HTTP status code â responses so far.

currentRps.description: Achieved RPS in the most recent bucket; null before the first bucket.

recentBuckets.description: Most recent 5-second buckets, oldest first (at most 12, i.e. one minute).

generatorSaturated.description: The load generator can't fire ticks at the configured rate (CPU-bound).

downstreamSaturated.description: Target p99 latency is approaching the request timeout (the target is the bottleneck).

flakyDispatch.description: A sustained share of dispatch batches are failing (agent or network).

ApiRunStatusResponse.description: Live state of the profile's current run. `IDLE` when nothing is running; a finished run reports `COMPLETED` with its final counters until the profile is started or stopped again. Final metrics and the verdict land in `/api/v1/history`.

t.description: Elapsed seconds at the middle of the bucket.

badRatio.description: Fraction of responses that were 4xx/5xx or connection failures.

RunStatusBucket.description: Most recent 5-second buckets, oldest first (at most 12, i.e. one minute).

ApiKeyAuth.description: API key prefixed with `tm_`. Issued from the in-app settings page.
ApiKeyAuth.name: X-Api-Key

BearerAuth.description: Same key as `X-Api-Key`, sent in the `Authorization: Bearer tm_â¦` form.
